outline.description: Sets out the executive actions that triggered the litigation, the parties, the district court’s preliminary injunctions, prior Ninth Circuit stay orders and carveouts, and the events leading to this interlocutory stay order.
subtopics: Executive Order 14163 (Realigning the United States Refugee Admissions Program): suspension of refugee entry under 8 U.S.C. §§ 1182(f), 1185(a)
State Department’s suspension of USRAP funding pursuant to Executive Order 14169 (Reevaluating and Realigning United States Foreign Aid)
Plaintiffs: refugees (admitted and approved but abroad) and three nonprofit organizations holding cooperative agreements for overseas processing and domestic resettlement services

District court preliminary injunctions: Feb. 25 oral order enjoining EO 14163 §§ 3(a)-(c), 4; Feb. 28 written order clarifying scope and barring funding suspension; Mar. 24 order requiring reinstatement of terminated cooperative agreements
Government’s post-injunction termination of all reception-and-placement cooperative agreements and nearly all overseas processing agreements; representation of an RFP for new providers

Ninth Circuit motions-panel stays: Mar. 25 partial stay with carveout for individuals conditionally approved before Jan. 20, 2025; Apr. 21 and May 9 clarifications; July 14 district court enforcement framework; July 17 emergency motion; July 18 administrative stay; Sept. 3 expedited argument

Current panel action: vacatur of prior stays (Mar. 25, Apr. 21, May 9; and July 18 administrative stay), stay of the district court’s Feb. 28 and Mar. 24 preliminary injunctions except as specified, and denial of the July 17 emergency motion as moot

outline.chapter_title: Governing Law: Entry Power, Refugee Resettlement Statutes, and the APA
outline.description: Explains the legal framework the court applies: presidential authority to suspend entry, the Refugee Act’s domestic services scheme and implementation mechanisms, appropriations context, and the APA backdrop for challenging agency actions.
subtopics: Presidential entry authority under 8 U.S.C. § 1182(f) and § 1185(a); deference principles from Trump v. Hawaii, 585 U.S. 667 (2018)
Refugee Act of 1980 domestic resettlement framework: 8 U.S.C. § 1522 (services for admitted refugees) and § 1523 (reporting/accountability)

Key statutory directives: § 1522(a)(1)(A) “shall” obligations (subject to available appropriations); § 1522(d)(2)(B) responsibilities for unaccompanied minors; § 1522(e)(7)(A) interim support and services for refugees <36 months in the U.S.
Implementing regulations: 45 C.F.R. §§ 400.200 et seq. (funding and services for refugees)
Mechanisms to deliver services: contracts, grants, or cooperative agreements with public or private nonprofits under § 1522(b)(1)(A)(ii)
Appropriations context: FY 2025 migration and refugee assistance funding and partial rescission; “to the extent of available appropriations” qualifier
APA framework as relevant: review of agency terminations of funding and cooperative agreements for consistency with statute and reasoned decisionmaking

outline.chapter_title: Stay Standard and Application to the Entry Suspension
outline.description: Sets out the Nken factors governing stays and details the panel’s application to the challenge against Executive Order 14163’s suspension of refugee admissions.
subtopics: Nken v. Holder four-factor test and primacy of likelihood of success and irreparable harm
Likelihood of success: reliance on Trump v. Hawaii; limited judicial inquiry into presidential findings under § 1182(f); clear textual fit of the EO
Irreparable harm, balance of equities, and public interest: weight given to foreign and domestic interests and broad executive discretion
Result under Nken: district court’s injunction against EO 14163’s entry suspension is stayed pending appeal

outline.chapter_title: Statutory Services After Admission: The Narrow Exception and APA Likelihood
outline.description: Explains why, despite staying the district court’s orders overall, the panel carved out a limited directive requiring the government to ensure domestic resettlement services for already-admitted refugees under § 1522.
subtopics: Preliminary merits assessment: government not likely to prevail on at least one APA claim tied to statutory obligations in § 1522

Statutory baseline: court’s reading that § 1522 requires provision of certain reception and placement services to admitted refugees, subject to appropriations and as outlined by statute and regulations
Record evidence: termination of cooperative agreements; government’s lack of progress in securing replacement capacity; existence of FY 2025 appropriations and statutory reporting duties under § 1523

Operative directive: government must reinstate cooperative agreements necessary to provide § 1522 services to refugees who have been admitted to the United States; services to include the usual and customary services under prior agreements
Relationship to broader stay: all district court preliminary injunctions remain stayed except for this appellate directive; prior carveout for conditionally approved refugees is vacated

outline.chapter_title: Judge Lee’s Partial Concurrence and Dissent: Authorization vs. Mandate in § 1522
outline.description: Presents Judge Lee’s competing interpretation of § 1522 as permissive, his critique of the majority’s statutory reading, and the remedial consequences he would adopt.
subtopics: Core disagreement: § 1522 as authorization to fund programs, not a mandate to operate them
Textual cues: section title “Authorization,” repeated “is authorized” phrasing in subsections (b)-(e), and Black’s Law definition of authorization
Reading § 1522(a): “shall” and “to the extent of available appropriations” as conditions that apply only if the government chooses to provide assistance
Subsections (d)(2)(B) and (e)(7)(A): “if necessary” and “as needed” as discretion-preserving, not imposing hard mandates
Remedy: would stay the district court’s injunctions in their entirety and not compel reinstatement of cooperative agreements

outline.chapter_title: Practical Effects and What to Watch on the Merits
outline.description: Summarizes the immediate operational consequences of the stay order and flags the key legal questions likely to shape the forthcoming merits opinion.
subtopics: Immediate effect: suspension of new refugee entries under EO 14163 continues; government must reinstate cooperative agreements to deliver standard § 1522 services to refugees admitted to the U.S.
Mootness disposition: government’s July 17 emergency motion denied as moot; prior stay orders vacated

Key merits issues ahead: scope of § 1182(f) deference; whether § 1522 imposes enforceable duties; interaction of appropriations limits with statutory service obligations; APA constraints on terminating service infrastructure
Doctrinal significance: separating sovereign entry control from Congress’s post-entry service mandates; limits of judicial review versus deference in national security and immigration administration
Next steps: panel opinion on the merits to issue; potential for further appellate review
